### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Meester-Loeys syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.762)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-3560783, Reactome:R-HSA-2022870, Reactome:R-HSA-2022923, Reactome:R-HSA-3560801, Reactome:R-HSA-3595177)

**Proposed mechanism:** Biglycan (HGNC:1044) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002650); Extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004322); Biglycan (HGNC:1044) —DISRUPTS→ Joint hypermobility (HP:0001382). Loss-of-function mutations in the BGN gene disrupt extracellular matrix organization, leading to skeletal dysplasia and short stature characteristic of X-linked spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia. Similarly, disruption of BGN function contributes to joint hypermobility seen in Meester-Loeys syndrome through its role in extracellular matrix integrity.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct causal genes for each disease in independent cohorts, or demonstration that mutations in BGN lead to gain-of-function effects in one disease while loss-of-function in the other. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic variants in BGN within gnomAD, suggesting these are extremely rare mutations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BGN in extracellular matrix homeostasis could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting matrix repair or modulation for both skeletal dysplasias and connective tissue disorders.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in BGN or HSPG2 in individuals with these phenotypes, or demonstration that genetic defects in these genes do not impact proteoglycan biosynthesis or extracellular matrix organization. _(variant: gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01 for pathogenic variants in BGN or HSPG2.)_
